evidence: The hunk drops the "invalid --json value" validation match and adds only "--output is no longer supported"; whether the new global --json=false rejection or a pflag unknown-flag message still lands in ExitValidation depends on message text the packet does not show. The PR merged at 20:52, five minutes before the 20:57 review, so the agent never had a chance to answer.
guidance_note: When removing an error message that ExitCode string-matches, grep ExitCode for that substring and add a test pinning the exit code of each input that used to produce it.

evidence: The new doc line says "`--json=false` is rejected" with no qualifier. In this era command-local flags were still stdlib flag.Bool (#43 later migrated them to Cobra), and flag.Bool accepts --json=false. The PR merged before the review landed, so the doc shipped wrong.
guidance_note: Before documenting that an input is rejected, run it through every parser that can see it (global pre-parse and each command-local FlagSet) and state the claim at the scope where it holds.

narrative: The agent merged a breaking CLI output-mode simplification one minute after opening the PR, five minutes before Copilot's only review. Both findings, an exit-code classification gap and an overstated doc claim about --json=false, went unanswered and shipped.
guidance_observations: Merging before the automated review posts makes every finding unanswerable; wait for the reviewer round before merging a behavior-changing PR.

evidence: The remediation says `lit migrate beads --apply --json`, but the reviewer reports that runMigrate rejects extra args and that BeadsMigrationRequiredError defaults to `lit migrate --apply --json`; the rename carried a stale `lnks migrate beads` string forward. The thread has no reply but is outdated and resolved after a second commit, so a silent fix is likely; the packet does not show that commit.
guidance_note: During a mechanical rename, check each remediation string the rename touches against the command's real usage instead of substituting the binary name in place.

evidence: The test pins the same nonexistent `lit migrate beads` invocation as F1, so it locks the wrong remediation in place. The thread is outdated and resolved with no reply; the packet does not show the fix.
guidance_note: A test that asserts a remediation command should assert the string the typed error actually emits, not a hand-copied literal.

narrative: This was a lnks-to-lit rename across 36 files. Copilot caught one remediation string, plus the test that pins it, that pointed at a nonexistent `migrate beads` subcommand. Both threads were resolved and made outdated with no reply.
guidance_observations: Resolving threads silently leaves no record of what changed; a one-line Fixed-in-sha reply would make the outcome checkable.

evidence: The reviewer assumed the default branch was `main`. The agent checked: "GitHub reports defaultBranchRef.name=master for this repo, and origin/HEAD points to origin/master", so `master` in the doc is accurate.

narrative: This is a design doc PR with a single finding, which wrongly claimed the default branch was main. The agent verified the real default branch and declined with evidence.
guidance_observations: The pushback cited a concrete, checkable fact (defaultBranchRef) instead of asserting the reviewer was wrong.

evidence: normalizeIssuePrefix has no length bound, and the prefix is embedded in issues.id VARCHAR(191). Only deriveIssuePrefix truncates to 12, so a hand-edited config bypasses the bound. The agent moved normalization and length enforcement into a shared internal/issueid boundary.
guidance_note: When a derived value has a bound (truncate to 12), apply the same bound wherever the value can enter from config, not only on the derivation path.

evidence: normalizeConfiguredIssuePrefix in the store duplicated the workspace normalizer, also without bounds. The agent routed both through the same issueid boundary and removed the hardcoded fallback, which fixes this finding and F1 together.
guidance_note: When writing a second normalizer for a value another package already normalizes, import the first one instead; two normalizers drift on validation rules.

evidence: The concern is real (one UPDATE per row, buffered in Go) but overstated for a local issue tracker's startup migration. The reviewer suggested set-based SQL, and the agent replaced the Go backfill with "a SQL reconciliation update", which also deletes code.

narrative: This PR added topic-based issue IDs. Two findings flagged the same unbounded-prefix gap from two duplicated normalizers, and the agent consolidated both into one package in a single fix commit. The third finding, on the row-by-row backfill, was fixed by switching to set-based SQL.
guidance_observations: Both the workspace and store packages grew their own prefix normalizer in the original PR; the review round was spent on that duplication.

evidence: printHelp calls fs.cmd.Flags().PrintDefaults(), but SetOutput only set the Cobra command writers, so pflag's own output was never redirected to helpOutput. The agent made SetOutput update "both the Cobra command writers and the underlying pflag writer".
guidance_note: When wrapping a library type that has two output sinks (Cobra command and its pflag FlagSet), redirect both in the wrapper's SetOutput and test that help text lands on the given writer.

evidence: cmd.Flags().SetInterspersed(false) makes pflag stop at the first positional argument. Stdlib flag behaved differently here, so commands that never check NArg() could silently ignore later flags. The thread is outdated and resolved with no reply. In #45 the reviewer still describes `fs.NArg() != 0` checks as the convention, but the packet does not show how this was handled.
guidance_note: When swapping a parser library, list its semantic defaults that differ from the old one (interspersed parsing, bool forms) and either preserve them or add the validation the old behavior made unnecessary.

narrative: This PR migrated stdlib flag parsing to a Cobra wrapper. Copilot found a help-output split between the Cobra and pflag writers, which was fixed, and a parsing-semantics change from disabling interspersed flags, which was resolved silently.
guidance_observations: A parser-migration PR should carry a behavior-parity test that runs the same argv through both parsers.

evidence: `defer readStore.Close()` drops the error, while the same test checks seed.Close(). The PR was closed unmerged and its work was redone in #48 and #49, so no response was given.
guidance_note: In tests, close stores via t.Cleanup with an error check, the same way other tests in the file do.

evidence: The finding depends on Store.Close() already mapping context.Canceled to nil, and the packet does not show Close's body. The PR was closed unmerged.
AGENTS.md was switched from `lit` to `lnks` after #40 had restored `lit` as the canonical name and made lnks only a compatibility symlink. The PR was closed unmerged.
guidance_note: Rebase a branch onto master before opening the PR, and diff docs against the canonical names master settled; this branch reverted #40's rename.

evidence: This is the same OpenForRead lock-plus-migrate concern as #48/F1. Readers really do serialize on the commit lock, but a separate schema probe would duplicate migrate's knowledge of the schema. The PR was closed unmerged.

quickstart reuses newBlockerAnnotator, which calls GetIssueDetail per open issue, an N+1 pattern. The agent later accepted the same finding in #49/F1 and replaced it with a bulk ListOpenBlockersForIssues query. This PR was closed unmerged.
guidance_note: Before reusing a per-item annotator on a hot command, check whether it does a store round-trip per item and batch the lookup first.

narrative: The PR was closed unmerged with no replies to any of its five findings. Its two halves were reopened as #48 (read-path migration) and #49 (quickstart not-ready summary), where two of these findings resurfaced: F4 as #48/F1 and F5 as #49/F1. F3 shows the branch also carried a stale AGENTS.md that undid #40's lit rename.
guidance_observations: Bundling two unrelated changes (store open semantics and a quickstart feature) into one PR led to closing it and redoing both halves, which paid for the same findings twice.

evidence: runFixPriority passed the raw *jsonOut instead of consulting shouldWriteJSON like the other commands. Commit 4c0fe4f adds `writeJSON := shouldWriteJSON(stdout, *jsonOut)` and routes output through printValue.
guidance_note: When adding a command, copy its output-mode plumbing from an existing command (shouldWriteJSON / printValue) instead of reading the local flag directly.

evidence: Without an fs.NArg() check, extra args after the issue id were silently accepted. 4c0fe4f adds `if fs.NArg() != 0 { return usage }`, matching the other commands. The reply was "will do".
guidance_note: When adding a command that uses splitArgs, include the fs.NArg() != 0 check the sibling commands carry.

evidence: The bash and fish command lists gained fix-priority but zsh did not. 4c0fe4f adds `'fix-priority:fix priority inversion on an issue'` to the zsh commands array.
guidance_note: When registering a new command in completions, update every shell's list in the same edit; grep for an existing command name such as 'update' to find all of them.

evidence: The reply said "We will remove the tests around this to make them all the same", but 4c0fe4f instead adds `{shell: "zsh", want: "fix-priority"}` exactly as the reviewer suggested. The code ended up right, but the stated plan, deleting coverage, was wrong and did not match the action.
The comment said P5 while the test sets Priority: 4 on a 0..4 scale. 4c0fe4f changes it to P4.
guidance_note: When writing a test comment that restates a fixture value, copy it from the fixture literal.

evidence: This is the same P5-versus-Priority: 4 mismatch as F5 in the second test, and 4c0fe4f fixes it there too.

The flag is a false positive: 4c0fe4f's ready_state.go diff touches only runFixPriority and the printPriorityChanges helpers, not newBlockerAnnotator. The removal of openDependencyIDs and sort.Strings came from the PR's original commit, which round 0 missed. The thread is resolved with no reply and is not outdated, so the packet does not show whether ordering was restored.
guidance_note: When rewriting a loop that consumed a sorted helper's output, keep the sort or say in the PR why ordering no longer matters.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the BFS loop calling Store.UpdateIssue per blocker existed in round 0, and 4c0fe4f only swapped its final output line for printValue. The thread is outdated and resolved with no reply, so the packet does not show what changed.
guidance_note: When a command mutates several records in one user action, check whether the store API commits per call and batch the updates into one transaction.

evidence: This is an organization preference, not a defect. The fix-priority command already lived in ready_state.go in round 0, and 4c0fe4f only edited it in place, so the flag is not fix-caused. The thread is outdated and resolved with no reply.
guidance_note: Put a new command in its own file when adding it, rather than in a sibling command's state file.

narrative: Round 0 raised six real but small findings: JSON mode, NArg validation, zsh completion and its test, and two P5 comment typos. 4c0fe4f fixed all of them, though the F4 reply announced deleting tests and the commit added the requested assertion instead. Round 1's three findings sit on code from the original commit that round 0 overlooked, not on anything 4c0fe4f changed, so the second round was not caused by a fix.
guidance_observations: Terse replies like "fine", "sure thing" and "will do" carry no plan, and in F4 the stated plan contradicted the commit; replies should name what the commit does.

evidence: Changing blockedByDef's key from "blocked_by" to "open_dependency" changes the --json payload, because Kind.MarshalJSON emits the key, which contradicts the PR description's claim that JSON is unchanged. The thread is outdated and resolved with no reply, so the packet does not show whether the description or the code changed.
guidance_note: When renaming a serialized enum key, check whether MarshalJSON emits it and call out the wire-format change in the PR description.

narrative: This PR replaced the blocked-ticket listing with a count summary and renamed an annotation kind key. The single finding correctly noted that the rename breaks the JSON contract the description said was unchanged. It was resolved silently.
guidance_observations: A PR description that asserts output compatibility should be checked against every serialized key the diff renames.

evidence: The hunk discards normalizeStatus's result (`if _, err := normalizeStatus(s)`) and appends the raw token, so `in-progress` would query a value that never matches. The agent fixed it to use the normalized value.
guidance_note: When converting a scalar field to a slice, carry the scalar path's normalize-then-use step into the loop; the `_` discard is the tell.

evidence: IssueTypes went straight into the IN clause untrimmed, while IDs were trimmed. The agent added TrimSpace and blank filtering at the store.
guidance_note: When adding multi-value filter fields, apply the same per-element normalization to each of them as the existing field (IDs) already gets.

evidence: This is the same untrimmed-IN-clause gap as F2, for Assignees, and it was fixed the same way in the same pass.

The exported ExecRaw bypasses the commit lock and commitWorkingSet. The agent renamed it ExecRawForTest instead of unexporting it, which only signals intent. The cli package's new orphan tests likely need cross-package access, which would rule out the suggested lowercase execRaw, but the packet does not show the callers.
printInProgressSection hardcoded " | " lines regardless of --format, while the Ready section uses printAnnotatedRows' format switch. The agent routed it through the same switch.
guidance_note: When adding an output section, render it through the existing format dispatch instead of writing one format inline.

evidence: Merge normalized only incoming.Statuses (`normalizeQueryStatuses(incoming.Statuses)`), so --status values in the base filter stayed raw. The agent normalized both sides.
applyTerm trimmed assignee, id and label values but appended `strings.TrimPrefix(term, "type:")` untrimmed. The agent added TrimSpace and blank skipping.
guidance_note: When rewriting one case of a term parser, diff it against the sibling cases for the normalization they share.

evidence: The new comment claimed "Direct writeJSON calls are forbidden outside this function" while runExport called writeJSON. The agent narrowed the comment to commands with both JSON and text modes, which matches the code after F9 made export JSON-only.
guidance_note: Before writing an absolute invariant into a comment ("forbidden outside this function"), grep for existing violations.

evidence: runExport wrapped writeJSON inside a textFn passed to printValue, so text mode still emitted JSON and the single-enforcer claim was false. The agent took the reviewer's first option and made export JSON-only.
guidance_note: When migrating call sites to a shared output helper, skip commands that have no text form instead of passing a textFn that emits JSON.

narrative: This PR converted scalar filters to slices, added an in-progress section and migrated output to printValue. Most of the nine findings were normalization the scalar code had and the slice conversion dropped (F1, F2, F3, F6, F7). All were fixed in one pass. F8 and F9 were resolved coherently: export became JSON-only, and the invariant comment was narrowed to match.
guidance_observations: Five of nine findings come from one refactor shape, scalar to slice, losing per-value normalization; one sweep over every converted field before opening the PR would have caught them.

evidence: The cost is real: readers now take the commit lock and serialize behind writers. The agent is right that a separate schema probe "duplicates knowledge about what constitutes a current schema". Its claim that "OpenForRead would already fail at openStoreConnection since Dolt needs write access" is not verifiable from the packet, and the PR also deletes the prior [LAW:single-enforcer] comment that read paths never migrate.
The test's information_schema query lacked `table_schema = DATABASE()`, unlike the existing migration probes the reviewer cites. The agent added the constraint.
guidance_note: When writing a test probe against information_schema, copy the schema-scoped form the production migrations already use.

narrative: This PR re-landed the OpenForRead auto-migrate half of closed #44. The agent declined the lock-on-read concern with a one-source-of-truth argument; one supporting claim, that Dolt already needs write access, is unverified in the packet. A test-probe scoping fix was applied.
guidance_observations: The pushback's factual leg (Dolt needs write access) was asserted, not shown; a pushback that rests on an environment fact should include the check that establishes it.

evidence: newBlockerAnnotator calls GetIssueDetail, which also loads comments and history, once per issue. The agent replaced it with a bulk `ListOpenBlockersForIssues` JOIN query. The same finding had been raised as #44/F5.
guidance_note: A finding left unanswered on a closed PR (#44/F5) should be fixed before the work is re-opened, not re-raised by the reviewer.

evidence: `if annotateErr == nil { payload["not_ready"] = ... }` silently omitted the section on failure, so consumers could not tell zero from not computed. The agent applied the suggested structured {"error": ...} payload.
guidance_note: Never write `if err == nil { use }` with no else; decide at write time whether the error propagates or is surfaced in the output.

evidence: In the same renderer, `summary` was rebound from the string summary field to a notReadySummary value. The agent renamed it `notReady`.

narrative: This PR re-landed the quickstart half of closed #44, and Copilot re-raised the N+1 annotator that #44/F5 had already flagged. All three findings were fixed, but the PR was later closed as obsoleted by #61's static quickstart.
guidance_observations: Re-opening work from a closed PR without first applying the closed PR's valid unanswered findings cost a repeat finding.

evidence: resetGlobalTemplate errors when the global path is empty, but the packet does not show whether Load calls ensureGlobalTemplate before checking the project template, so the claim that Load fails even when a valid project template exists is unverified. Failing loudly when there is no config directory is consistent with the PR's stated "enforce global reset semantics". The thread was resolved with no reply.

`defaultsFS.ReadFile(filepath.Join("defaults", name))` uses OS separators, but embed.FS paths are always slash-separated, so this breaks on Windows. The thread was resolved with no reply and is not outdated, so the line shipped unchanged.
guidance_note: Use path.Join, never filepath.Join, for any embed.FS or io/fs path.

narrative: This PR externalized managed templates. Copilot raised an empty-global-path failure mode, unverifiable from the packet, and a real filepath.Join-on-embed.FS portability bug. Both threads were resolved with no reply, and neither line is marked outdated.
guidance_observations: Resolving a thread with no reply and no code change discards a correct finding without a recorded reason.
